subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Clock Signals: The Heartbeat of Digital Circuits
description: A micro-lesson that makes Clock Signals: The Heartbeat of Digital Circuits usable.

hook.text: A clock signal toggles between 0 and 1 at a fixed rate. It's the heartbeat of every chip.

buildup.text: At each clock edge, flip-flops capture data, counters increment, and state machines advance.

discovery.text: Clock speed is measured in hertz. A 4 GHz processor ticks four billion times per second.

twist.text: Higher clock speed generates more heat. Modern chips throttle speed to manage thermal limits.

climax.text: Clock distribution networks span entire chips — ensuring every flip-flop ticks in sync.

punchline.text: No clock, no sync, no computing — the clock is the pulse that keeps order.

quiz.question: Why do faster clock speeds generate more heat?
options: More clock edges per second means more transistor switching, which dissipates energy as heat
The clock signal itself carries more voltage at higher frequencies
Faster clocks create electromagnetic radiation that heats nearby components
